label: Federated tenant posture
query: What should Lakeshore L0 see that Morgan Street L1 should not automatically see at transaction grain?
answer: At transaction grain, I’d draw the line this way: Lakeshore L0 (enterprise / holdco) should automatically see: 1) Group‑level control fields – Full legal‑entity hierarchy and roll‑ups (all opcos, JVs, SPEs) – Counterparty master with full KYC/KYB, internal risk ratings, sanctions flags – Internal entity/desk/strategy codes that show “who is trading with whom” inside the group – Enterprise identifiers that link the same external counterparty across banners and entities 2) Treasury / risk / control attributes – Cash/pool allocations and sweeping logic across entities – Internal transfer pricing, funding spreads, cost‑of‑funds tags – Liquidity, concentration, and limit‑utilization fields at entity and group level – Model/risk identifiers used for VaR, stress, and capital attribution 3) Sensitive control metadata – User / desk / system IDs, approvals and 4‑eyes controls, exception codes – Full booking source, enrichment path, and data‑quality flags Morgan Street L1 (business‑line) should not automatically see: – Any cross‑entity “who else is transacting” view beyond their accountable entity perimeter – Lake­shore‑wide counterparty exposure and limits, only what’s relevant to their legal entity/desk – Internal transfer‑pricing and funding economics not baked into their official P&L – Other opcos’ positions, hedges, or liquidity that aren’t contractually shared – Group‑level KYC notes, risk‑review narratives, or investigative flags that aren’t specific to their book The decision you need to make next is: where exactly do you draw “perimeter = legal entity vs. business line vs. desk” and encode that as row‑level security policy.
